senses.def: strange and frightening because it is connected with death
ex: The film has a macabre ending.
They found macabre objects in the cellar.

senses.def: silly or very strange (informal)
ex: You're mad to go out in this storm.
What a mad idea!

senses.def: angry (informal)
ex: My mum is mad at me.
He was mad about the broken window.

senses.def: a polite way to speak to a woman, especially in a shop or formal letter
ex: Can I help you, madam?
Dear Madam, I am writing to complain.

senses.def: a French title for a married woman, equal to Mrs
ex: Madame Dupont is the head of the school.
Please welcome Madame Rousseau.

senses.def: very silly or dangerous behaviour
ex: It's madness to drive so fast.
The plan was pure madness.

senses.def: a serious mental illness (old-fashioned)
ex: The king fell into madness.

senses.def: a very strong whirlpool in water, or a confusing situation
ex: The boat was sucked into the maelstrom.
She was caught in a maelstrom of emotions.

senses.def: a very skilled musician, especially a conductor
ex: The maestro raised his baton.
The young pianist studied with a famous maestro.

senses.def: the young form of a fly, which looks like a small worm
ex: Maggots were in the rubbish bin.
Fishermen sometimes use maggots as bait.

senses.def: having special powers that seem impossible
ex: She has a magic wand.
It's a magic carpet that flies.

senses.def: a special power that makes impossible things happen
ex: The witch used magic to change the prince into a frog.
The story is full of magic.

senses.def: clever tricks that seem impossible, done to entertain
ex: He does magic at children's parties.

senses.def: very special and exciting, as if by magic
ex: It was a magical evening.
The island is a magical place.

senses.def: a person who does magic tricks to entertain people
ex: The magician pulled a rabbit from his hat.
We hired a magician for the party.

senses.def: a person in stories who has magic powers
ex: The magician cast a spell on the village.

senses.def: kind and forgiving, especially to an enemy
ex: The winner was magnanimous in victory.
It was a magnanimous gesture to forgive him.

senses.def: a rich and powerful person in business
ex: He is a shipping magnate.
The oil magnate gave money to the university.

senses.def: having the power to pull iron or steel towards it
ex: The Earth has a magnetic field.
Magnetic tape stored the sound.

senses.def: having a quality that strongly attracts people
ex: He has a magnetic personality.

senses.def: the force that attracts iron and steel, or a strong personal attraction
ex: Magnetism is used in many machines.
Her personal magnetism drew the crowd.

senses.def: extremely beautiful or impressive
ex: We had a magnificent view of the sea.
It was a magnificent performance.

senses.def: a black and white bird with a long tail that likes shiny things
ex: A magpie stole the ring from the table.
Magpies built a nest in the tree.

senses.def: a box outside a house or in the street where letters are delivered or posted
ex: There was a letter in the mailbox.
He dropped the card in the mailbox.

senses.def: the part of an email account where messages arrive
ex: My mailbox is full.

senses.def: most important or largest
ex: The main road is closed.
What is your main reason for coming?

senses.def: to keep something in good condition or at the same level
ex: The city must maintain its roads.
Try to maintain a healthy weight.

senses.def: to state strongly that something is true
ex: He maintains that he is innocent.

senses.def: the work of keeping something in good condition
ex: The road is closed for maintenance.
Car maintenance can be expensive.

senses.def: very large or important
ex: There was a major problem with the plan.
It is a major city.

senses.def: the main subject that a student studies at university
ex: Her major is biology.
What was your major at college?

senses.def: most of the people or things in a group
ex: The majority of students passed.
The majority voted in favour.

mistake.wrong: The majority of people is happy.
mistake.right: The majority of people are happy.
mistake.note: After majority of + plural noun, use a plural verb.

senses.def: to produce, build or prepare something
ex: She makes cakes.
They make cars in this factory.

senses.def: to cause someone or something to do or become something
ex: The film made me cry.
The news made her happy.

senses.def: the name of the company that produces a product
ex: What make is your phone?
This is a well-known make of car.

mistake.note: After make, use the base verb without to.

senses.def: a serious disease caused by the bite of some mosquitoes
ex: Many travellers take pills against malaria.
Malaria is common in some hot countries.

senses.def: a person or animal that is not female
ex: The police are looking for a male in a black coat.
Most of the birds were males.

senses.def: being a man or boy, or connected with them
ex: He is a male nurse.
The male lion has a large mane.

senses.def: to fail to work correctly
ex: The machine malfunctioned and stopped.
The alarm malfunctioned during the night.

senses.def: a wish to hurt or upset someone
ex: He spoke without malice.
She felt no malice towards him.

senses.def: intended to hurt or upset someone
ex: They spread malicious rumours.
He sent a malicious email.

senses.def: in a way that is intended to hurt or upset someone
ex: She smiled maliciously.
He maliciously damaged the car.

senses.def: easy to bend or shape, or easy to influence
ex: Gold is a malleable metal.
Young minds are malleable.

senses.def: a mother (informal, used by children)
ex: Mama, can I have a biscuit?
The baby called for his mama.

senses.def: an adult male person
ex: The man opened the door.
Two men were waiting outside.

senses.def: to operate a machine or work at a place
ex: Volunteers manned the phones all night.
The desk is manned 24 hours a day.

mistake.note: The plural of man is men.

senses.def: to succeed in doing something difficult
ex: I managed to finish the report.
She managed to open the box.

senses.def: to be in charge of a business or group
ex: He manages a hotel.
She manages a team of ten people.

mistake.wrong: He managed to passed the test.
mistake.right: He managed to pass the test.
mistake.note: Manage is followed by to + base verb.

senses.def: the control and organisation of a business
ex: Good management is important for success.
She works in hotel management.

senses.def: the people who run a business
ex: The management has agreed to raise pay.

senses.def: a person who is in charge of a shop, team or business
ex: The manager spoke to the staff.
She is the bank manager.

senses.def: to move something carefully into a different position
ex: The driver manoeuvred the lorry into the narrow gap.
The ship manoeuvred around the rocks.

senses.def: to guide a situation or person cleverly to get what you want
ex: She manoeuvred him into signing the deal.

senses.def: a careful or skilled movement
ex: The pilot made a difficult manoeuvre.
Parking in this small space needs a tricky manoeuvre.

senses.def: a clever action to gain an advantage
ex: The politician's last manoeuvre failed.

senses.def: to damage something badly by crushing or twisting it
ex: The machine mangled his sleeve.
The car was mangled in the crash.

senses.def: a sweet tropical fruit with a large stone and yellow-orange flesh
ex: I drank a glass of mango juice.
She peeled a ripe mango.

senses.def: a treatment to make your hands and nails look nice
ex: She had a manicure before the wedding.
A manicure takes about an hour.

senses.def: to cut, shape and paint someone's nails
ex: The beautician manicured her nails.
He manicured his nails carefully.

senses.def: to control or influence someone or something in a clever, often unfair way
ex: He manipulated her into giving him money.
The company manipulated the figures.

senses.def: to handle or use something skilfully
ex: The surgeon manipulated the tiny tools carefully.

senses.def: the act of controlling someone or something in a clever, often unfair way
ex: The report found manipulation of the results.
She was a victim of emotional manipulation.

senses.def: all people, thought of together
ex: Fire was a great discovery for mankind.
The invention changed the life of mankind.

senses.def: a very large, grand house
ex: The film star lives in a mansion.
They sold the old mansion for millions.

senses.def: done with the hands, not with a machine
ex: Digging is hard manual work.
He has a manual gearbox in his car.

senses.def: a book that tells you how to use or fix something
ex: Read the manual before using the machine.
The car manual is in the glove box.

senses.def: the production of goods in large numbers, usually by machine
ex: The manufacture of cars is a big industry.
Several firms are involved in the manufacture of paper.

senses.def: to make goods in large numbers, usually in a factory
ex: The company manufactures furniture.
These shoes are manufactured in Turkey.

senses.def: a company that makes goods in large numbers
ex: The manufacturer offers a two-year guarantee.
He works for a car manufacturer.

senses.def: the business of making goods in large numbers
ex: Manufacturing is important to the economy.
She has a job in manufacturing.

senses.def: a large number of people or things
ex: I don't have many friends here.
How many books have you read?

senses.def: a large number of people or things
ex: Many of the students were late.
Many have already left.

mistake.right: I have a lot of money.
mistake.note: Many is used with plural countable nouns, not uncountable nouns like money.

senses.def: a long running race of about 42 kilometres
ex: He ran the Paris marathon.
She is training for a marathon.

senses.def: any very long activity that needs a lot of effort
ex: The film was a three-hour marathon.
The talks turned into a marathon negotiation.

senses.def: a hard, often white stone used for buildings and statues
ex: The floor was made of marble.
The statue is carved from marble.

senses.def: a small glass ball used in a children's game
ex: The boys played marbles in the yard.
He lost a blue marble.

senses.def: the empty space at the edge of a page
ex: She wrote notes in the margin.
Leave a wide margin on each side.

senses.def: the amount by which something is won or achieved
ex: They won by a small margin.
There is little margin for error.

senses.def: connected with the sea and the things that live in it
ex: Marine animals include whales and fish.
She studies marine biology.

senses.def: a sailor
ex: The old mariner told stories of storms at sea.
Mariners used stars to find their way.

senses.def: a small area of dirt or damage on a surface
ex: There is a mark on my shirt.
Her fingers left marks on the glass.

senses.def: a number or letter that shows how good your work is
ex: She got a good mark in maths.
Marks are posted on Friday.

senses.def: to write or draw a sign on something
ex: Mark the correct answer with a cross.
He marked the map with a red pen.

senses.def: to check students' work and give it a mark
ex: The teacher marked the tests.
I have forty essays to mark.

senses.def: very clear and easy to notice
ex: There was a marked improvement in her work.
There is a marked difference between the two.

senses.def: a place where people buy and sell things, often outdoors
ex: We buy fruit at the market.
The market is open on Saturdays.

senses.def: the business of buying and selling a type of goods
ex: The housing market is slow.
The company wants a share of the market.

senses.def: to advertise and sell a product
ex: The firm markets its products worldwide.
The drink is marketed to teenagers.

senses.def: the business of advertising and selling products
ex: She works in marketing.
The company spends a lot on marketing.

senses.def: the legal relationship between a husband and a wife, or the ceremony of marrying
ex: Their marriage lasted fifty years.
Marriage is a big step.

senses.def: having a husband or wife
ex: They have been married for ten years.
She's married to a doctor.

mistake.wrong: She is married with a doctor. / He married with her.
mistake.right: She is married to a doctor. / He married her.
mistake.note: married to (adjective); marry + person, with no preposition. متزوج من is not married with.

senses.def: to become the husband or wife of someone
ex: She married a doctor.
They married in June.

mistake.note: Marry takes a direct object; use get married to or marry + person, not married with.

senses.def: to feel great surprise or admiration
ex: We marvelled at the beauty of the mountains.
She marvelled at his skill.

senses.def: something that causes great surprise or admiration
ex: The Pyramids are a marvel of engineering.
The clock is a marvel of design.

senses.def: something that covers your face to hide or protect it
ex: The thief wore a mask.
Doctors wear masks in the operating room.

senses.def: something that hides your true feelings
ex: His smile was a mask for his sadness.

senses.def: involving or affecting a large number of people
ex: The country faced mass unemployment.
Television is a mass medium.

senses.def: a large amount of something, often without a clear shape
ex: A mass of dark cloud covered the sky.
He had masses of work to do.

senses.def: a Christian church service
ex: They go to mass every Sunday.

senses.def: the killing of many people in a cruel way
ex: The massacre shocked the world.
Villagers fled to escape the massacre.

senses.def: the action of rubbing the body to ease pain or help it relax
ex: She had a back massage.
A massage can relieve muscle pain.

senses.def: to rub and press the body with your hands
ex: He massaged her sore shoulders.
Massage the oil gently into your skin.

senses.def: very big, heavy or serious
ex: They built a massive bridge.
There was a massive explosion.

senses.def: a person who is highly skilled at something
ex: He is a master of the guitar.
The painter was a master of colour.

senses.def: a man who owns or controls an animal or servant
ex: The dog ran to its master.

senses.def: an excellent piece of art, music or writing
ex: The painting is a masterpiece.
Many consider this novel his masterpiece.

senses.def: a friend (informal, mainly British)
ex: I'm going out with my mates tonight.
He is my best mate.

senses.def: an animal's partner for producing young
ex: The male bird looks for a mate.
Wolves keep the same mate for life.

senses.def: a substance that something is made from
ex: Wood is a building material.
What material is the bag made of?

senses.def: cloth used for making clothes
ex: She chose a blue material for the dress.
The curtains are made of thick material.

senses.def: the belief that money and possessions are the most important things
ex: Materialism is common in rich societies.
Some critics blame advertising for materialism.

senses.def: caring too much about money and possessions
ex: She is not materialistic.
Modern society is very materialistic.

senses.def: to happen or appear as expected
ex: The money never materialised.
The threat did not materialise.

senses.def: connected with being a mother, or relating to your mother's side of the family
ex: She has strong maternal instincts.
My maternal grandmother lives in Cairo.

senses.def: connected with mathematics
ex: It is a difficult mathematical problem.
She has a mathematical mind.

senses.def: the study of numbers, shapes and amounts
ex: He studies mathematics at university.
Mathematics is a required subject.

senses.def: a subject or situation that you are thinking about or dealing with
ex: It is a matter of life and death.
That is a private matter.

senses.def: used in what's the matter to ask about a problem
ex: What's the matter?
There is something the matter with the car.

senses.def: to be important
ex: Your health matters most.
It doesn't matter if you are late.

mistake.note: Matter takes to before the person, not for.

senses.def: behaving in a sensible, adult way, or fully grown
ex: She is very mature for her age.
The tree is mature.

senses.def: fully developed, as in a plant, animal or cheese
ex: A mature cheese has a strong taste.

senses.def: a person who thinks and acts in an independent way
ex: He was a maverick in the company.
The maverick director ignored the studio's advice.

senses.def: the largest amount or number (short for maximum)
ex: The room holds ten people, max.
Max speed is 90 kilometres an hour.

senses.def: as great or as large as possible
ex: The maximum speed is 50 miles an hour.
Take the maximum dose.

senses.def: the largest amount or number that is possible
ex: Five is the maximum I can carry.
The temperature will reach a maximum of 35 degrees.

senses.def: used to say that something is possible
ex: It may rain later.
She may be at home.

senses.def: used to ask or give permission politely
ex: May I come in?
You may leave now.

senses.def: the fifth month of the year
ex: My birthday is in May.
School ends in May.

senses.def: used when something is possible but not sure
ex: Maybe we will go to the beach.
Maybe he is ill.

mistake.note: May be is two words (modal + verb); maybe is one word and means perhaps.

senses.def: the person who is chosen to lead a town or city
ex: The mayor opened the new library.
She was elected mayor last year.

senses.def: used by the speaker to refer to themselves as the object of a verb or preposition
ex: Give me the book.
Come with me.

mistake.note: Use I, not me, for the subject of a sentence, and put the other person first.

senses.def: too small in amount
ex: He lived on a meagre income.
They ate a meagre dinner of bread.

senses.def: to have a particular sense, or to express an idea
ex: What does this word mean?
"Hola" means "hello" in Spanish.

senses.def: to plan or intend to do something
ex: I didn't mean to hurt you.
She meant to call but forgot.

senses.def: unkind or unpleasant to others
ex: Don't be mean to your sister.
It was a mean thing to say.

senses.def: the average of a set of numbers
ex: The mean of 2, 4 and 6 is 4.
Calculate the mean of the results.

senses.def: what a word, sign or action expresses
ex: What is the meaning of this word?
The sentence has two possible meanings.

senses.def: the importance or purpose of something
ex: He found new meaning in life.
The ceremony had a deep meaning for them.

senses.def: having a clear purpose or importance
ex: She wanted a meaningful job.
They had a meaningful talk.

senses.def: having no meaning or purpose
ex: The numbers were meaningless to me.
Life felt meaningless without her.

senses.def: a way of doing something
ex: Email is a quick means of communication.
The police found a means to enter the house.

senses.def: money or wealth
ex: He does not have the means to buy a house.
She lives within her means.

senses.def: during the time something else is happening
ex: Cook the rice. Meanwhile, chop the onions.
She was studying. Meanwhile, he was playing games.

senses.def: an official action taken to deal with a problem
ex: The government took measures to cut crime.
Safety measures are important.

senses.def: a unit or a way of judging the size of something
ex: A kilometre is a measure of distance.
Exams are one measure of success.

senses.def: to find the size, amount or degree of something
ex: Measure the length of the table.
The nurse measured his height.

senses.def: a person whose job is to repair machines, especially cars
ex: The mechanic fixed my car.
He works as a mechanic.

senses.def: connected with machines or working by machine
ex: A mechanical fault stopped the train.
The toy is mechanical, not electric.

senses.def: done without thinking, like a machine
ex: He answered in a mechanical way.

senses.def: a set of parts in a machine that does a particular job
ex: The lock has a simple mechanism.
The watch's mechanism is very small.

senses.def: a way in which something works or is done
ex: The body has a mechanism for fighting disease.

senses.def: television, radio, newspapers and the internet, thought of as a group
ex: The media reported the story widely.
Social media is popular with teenagers.

senses.def: to try to end a disagreement between two sides
ex: A judge mediated between the two firms.
The UN tried to mediate the dispute.

senses.def: the act of trying to settle a disagreement between people
ex: The two sides agreed to mediation.
The strike ended through mediation.

senses.def: connected with medicine and treating illness
ex: She needs urgent medical care.
He is a medical student.

senses.def: a drug or medicine used to treat illness
ex: She takes medication for her heart.
Ask your doctor about the medication.

senses.def: connected with the Middle Ages, about 500 to 1500
ex: They visited a medieval castle.
The town has a medieval church.

senses.def: not very good; of only average quality
ex: The food was mediocre.
He was a mediocre student.

senses.def: the quality of being only average or not very good
ex: The team was stuck in mediocrity.
They refused to accept mediocrity.

senses.def: the practice of staying quiet and calm for a time to relax or think
ex: She does meditation every morning.
Yoga and meditation help me relax.

senses.def: the sea between southern Europe and North Africa (the Mediterranean)
ex: We spent our holiday on the Mediterranean.
Many tourists visit the Mediterranean in summer.

senses.def: not big and not small; of middle size
ex: I'd like a medium coffee, please.
She is of medium height.

senses.def: a means used for communicating or showing something
ex: Television is a powerful medium.
Paint is her favourite medium.

senses.def: to see and talk to someone for the first time
ex: I met her at a party.
Nice to meet you.

senses.def: to come together with someone at a planned time
ex: Let's meet at the station at six.
We meet every Friday.

senses.def: a feeling of deep, quiet sadness
ex: There was a deep melancholy in his songs.
She sank into melancholy.

senses.def: quietly and deeply sad
ex: The melancholy music made her cry.
He looked melancholy.

senses.def: having a pleasant sound, like music
ex: The birds sang with melodious voices.
She has a melodious voice.

senses.def: a tune, or the main line of a piece of music
ex: The song has a beautiful melody.
She hummed the melody.

senses.def: to change from solid to liquid because of heat
ex: The snow melts in spring.
Melt the butter in a pan.

senses.def: a person who belongs to a group or organisation
ex: She is a member of the club.
He is a family member.

senses.def: an animal, plant or thing that is part of a group
ex: The lion is a member of the cat family.

senses.def: the state of being a member of a group, or the members themselves
ex: I pay for gym membership.
Membership of the club costs £20 a year.

senses.def: a statue or building that reminds people of a person or an event
ex: There is a memorial to the soldiers in the park.
They built a memorial for the victims.

senses.def: a person or thing that is dangerous or very annoying
ex: Drunk drivers are a menace.
The dog is a menace to the postman.

senses.def: seeming likely to cause harm
ex: A menacing figure stood in the doorway.
He gave her a menacing look.

senses.def: to repair something that is broken or torn
ex: Can you mend my shirt?
He mended the broken chair.

senses.def: boring and unskilled, and having low status
ex: He did menial jobs to pay for school.
She hated the menial work in the kitchen.

senses.def: connected with the mind
ex: Mental health is as important as physical health.
He did a quick mental calculation.

senses.def: in the mind, or in a way that affects the mind
ex: She was mentally tired after the exam.
He is mentally ill.

senses.def: a short comment about someone or something
ex: The report made no mention of the accident.
There was a brief mention of her name.

senses.def: to say something briefly
ex: She mentioned that she was tired.
He didn't mention the price.

mistake.note: Mention takes a direct object with no preposition.

senses.def: an experienced person who gives help and advice to a less experienced one
ex: My mentor taught me how to write well.
She found a mentor at her first job.

senses.def: connected with trade and business
ex: The port grew thanks to mercantile activity.
Mercantile law deals with business matters.

senses.def: a soldier who fights for any country or group that pays him
ex: The king hired mercenaries to fight the war.
Mercenaries are paid, not loyal.

senses.def: goods that are bought and sold
ex: The shop sells football merchandise.
Check the merchandise before you pay.

senses.def: a person who buys and sells goods in large quantities
ex: He was a wine merchant.
Merchants brought spices from the East.

senses.def: kindness shown by not punishing someone who has done wrong
ex: The judge showed no mercy.
The prisoners begged for mercy.

senses.def: used to emphasise that something is small or unimportant
ex: She is a mere child.
The mere thought of it makes me ill.

senses.def: only, and nothing more
ex: I was merely asking.
He is merely a beginner.

senses.def: to combine to form one thing
ex: The two banks merged last year.
The roads merge near the bridge.

senses.def: the joining of two companies to form one
ex: The merger created a huge firm.
The merger of the banks was announced today.

senses.def: a good quality that deserves praise
ex: The plan has many merits.
She won on merit.

senses.def: to deserve something
ex: The idea merits further study.
His efforts merit praise.

senses.def: to fit or work well together
ex: Their ideas meshed perfectly.
The gears mesh smoothly.

senses.def: a dirty or untidy state
ex: The kitchen is a mess.
Don't make a mess!

senses.def: to make something dirty or untidy
ex: Who messed up my room?
Don't mess with the controls.

senses.def: a person who takes a message to someone
ex: A messenger delivered the letter.
The king sent a messenger to the city.

senses.def: dirty or not tidy
ex: His room is always messy.
Painting can be a messy activity.

senses.def: a hard, shiny material such as iron or gold
ex: The bridge is made of metal.
Iron and copper are metals.

senses.def: a word or phrase that describes something by comparing it to something else
ex: "Time is money" is a metaphor.
The poet uses a metaphor for love.

senses.def: something used to represent an idea
ex: The storm is a metaphor for his anger.

senses.def: connected with the weather and the study of it
ex: The meteorological office predicts snow.
Meteorological data show a warmer year.

senses.def: done in a careful, organised way
ex: She is a methodical worker.
He made a methodical search of the house.

senses.def: the methods used in a particular activity or area of study
ex: The report explains the research methodology.
The team used a new methodology.

senses.def: very careful and exact about details
ex: She is meticulous in her work.
He kept meticulous records.

senses.def: in a very careful and exact way
ex: The room was meticulously clean.
He meticulously planned each detail.

senses.def: a device that makes sounds louder or records them
ex: The singer stepped up to the microphone.
He spoke into the microphone.

senses.def: a tool that makes very small things look bigger
ex: She looked at the cells under a microscope.
The school bought a new microscope.

senses.def: too small to be seen without a microscope
ex: Bacteria are microscopic.
The insects were microscopic.

senses.def: an oven that cooks food quickly using special waves
ex: Heat the soup in the microwave.
We bought a new microwave.

senses.def: twelve o'clock at night
ex: The film ended at midnight.
We stayed up until midnight.

senses.def: the middle of a situation or group (in the midst of)
ex: We are in the midst of a crisis.
She appeared in the midst of the crowd.

senses.def: a person trained to help women give birth
ex: The midwife helped deliver the baby.
She trained to be a midwife.

senses.def: used to say that something is possible but not certain
ex: It might rain tomorrow.
He might be late.

senses.def: used to make a polite suggestion
ex: You might want to call him.

senses.def: very strong or powerful
